name: Oil Pump Assembly for Husqvarna 395XP
title: Husqvarna 395XP Oil Pump Assembly: Fit & Replacement
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 395XP oil pump assembly for a big saw that has stopped oiling the bar. Signs of a bad pump, what to check first, and typical price.
tagline: Replacement bar-oil pump for the Husqvarna 395XP when the bar runs dry.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP oil pump assembly replaces the pump that feeds bar oil to the guide bar and chain. If the bar smokes, the chain turns blue, or no oil line shows on a stump when you rev the saw, a worn or damaged pump is one of the likely causes.
highlights: Replacement bar-oil pump for the 395XP
Restores oil flow to bar and chain
Fixes dry-running bars once clogs are ruled out
Shop-level repair with basic tools
specs: Bar and chain oil pump assembly

p: A 395XP pulls long bars in big wood, so oil delivery matters. Before you replace the pump, rule out the easy stuff: clear the oil hole in the bar pad and the bar groove, check the oil tank filter and pickup line, and make sure you are running clean bar oil. Sawdust packed around the clutch side is a common culprit.
If oil still does not reach the bar, the pump itself may be worn, cracked, or have a stripped drive. That is when this assembly earns its place on the bench.

A pump that has been run dry or fed dirty oil wears faster, so once it is replaced, keep the tank cap seal in good shape and fill from a clean container. Sawdust and grit that get into the tank end up in the pump.

Swapping the pump means pulling the clutch and working on the drive side of the saw, so it suits a mechanic or a crew member comfortable with saw repair. Use a piston stop and the right clutch tool, and replace the oil line or seals if they are hard or cracked while you are in there.

Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. More saw parts are in our chainsaw parts section.

faq.q: How do I know the 395XP oil pump is bad?
faq.a: If the oil tank is full, the bar oil hole and tank filter are clear, and the saw still throws no oil off the chain at high revs, the pump or its drive is the likely fault.

faq.q: Can I adjust the oil flow on a 395XP?
faq.a: Many Husqvarna pro saws have an adjustable oil pump. Check the operator's manual for your saw before turning any adjustment screw.

name: Oil Pump Assembly for Husqvarna 550XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Oil Pump Assembly
h1: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II Oil Pump Assembly
meta: Husqvarna 550XP Mark II oil pump assembly for a saw that won't oil the bar. What to check before replacing it, fitting tips and the typical street price.
tagline: Replacement bar-oil pump for the Husqvarna 550XP Mark II ground saw.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP Mark II oil pump assembly replaces the pump that meters bar oil to the chain on one of the most common ground saws in tree work. When the chain runs dry and the oil passages are clear, the pump is the next thing to look at.
highlights: Replacement oil pump for the 550XP Mark II
Gets bar oil back to the chain
Protects bar and chain from heat wear
Repair the saw instead of retiring it
specs: Bar and chain oil pump assembly

p: A 550XP Mark II gets used hard: limbing, bucking, and cleaning up after a takedown all day. When the bar starts smoking or the chain dulls fast, first pull the bar and clean the oil hole, the bar groove, and the area around the clutch cover. Check the tank filter and oil hose for clogs or cracks.
If oil still does not show when you hold the running saw over a light-colored stump, the pump is likely worn or damaged and this assembly is the fix.
Bar oil that is too thick in cold weather can also slow delivery, so match your oil to the season before blaming the pump. A winter-grade bar oil flows better on frosty mornings.

The pump sits behind the clutch, so plan on removing the clutch with the correct tool and a piston stop. Inspect the worm drive and oil line while it is apart and replace anything worn. Run the saw and confirm a steady oil line before it goes back on a job.

Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. Browse more chainsaw parts for the 550XP.

faq.q: Is the Mark II pump the same as the original 550XP?
faq.a: Not always. The Mark II has its own parts list, so confirm the part number for your exact model before ordering.

faq.q: Why does my 550XP oil fine at idle but not under load?
faq.a: Check for a partly blocked bar oil hole or a pinched oil line first. If those are clear, a worn pump drive can lose output as the saw works.

name: Outer Felling Dog for Husqvarna 572XP
title: Husqvarna 572XP Felling Dog, Outer (Bucking Spike)
meta: Replacement outer Husqvarna 572XP felling dog, the spiked bumper that pivots the saw in big wood. Why to replace a worn one, how it mounts, and typical cost.
tagline: Replacement outer bucking spike for the Husqvarna 572XP.
summary: This outer Husqvarna 572XP felling dog is the toothed spike that bolts to the front of the saw and gives the bar something to pivot on while felling and bucking. Worn or bent dogs slip on bark, which makes cuts slower and less controlled.
highlights: Replacement outer spike for the 572XP
Gives the saw a solid pivot in big wood
Helps control cuts when felling and bucking
Simple bolt-on swap

p: On a 70cc-class saw like the 572XP, the felling dogs do a lot of work. Planting the spikes and pivoting the saw lets you pull through a big log with the saw's weight instead of your back, and it keeps the saw from walking when you bore or set a back cut.
Teeth wear down on bark, dirt, and the occasional rock, and an outer dog can bend if the saw gets dropped or pinched. A rounded dog slips, and a slipping saw is harder to control.
Some climbers and fallers prefer an aggressive dog for big hardwood, and a worn stock dog is the first thing to check if the saw feels like it is skating across the bark instead of biting in.
The outer dog mounts to the saw body with screws on the bar side. Remove the bar and chain, swap the dog, torque the screws snug, and check that nothing contacts the chain path before you reassemble.

While the bar is off, clean the bar pad, check the chain catcher, and look at the clutch cover for cracks. Small parts like the dogs and chain catcher are cheap and quick to replace, and a saw that holds its position in the cut is safer to run.

Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. Find more Husqvarna saw parts here.

faq.q: What does a felling dog do?
faq.a: It is a spiked bumper at the base of the bar. You plant it in the wood and pivot the saw on it, which gives more control and less effort in larger cuts.

faq.q: Do I need the inner dog too?
faq.a: Some saws use an inner and outer dog together. Replace whichever is worn, and check that both match your saw's parts list.

name: Recoil Starter Handle for Husqvarna 500 Series Chainsaws
title: Husqvarna Starter Handle for 500 Series Chainsaws
h1: Husqvarna Starter Handle for 500 Series Chainsaws
meta: Replacement Husqvarna starter handle for 500 series chainsaws. Fix a cracked or missing pull grip in minutes, with tips on rewinding the cord and typical price.
tagline: Replacement pull grip for Husqvarna 500 series chainsaw starters.
summary: This Husqvarna starter handle is the pull grip for the recoil starter on 500 series chainsaws. Handles crack from cold, sun, and being slapped against the saw housing, and a broken one makes a hot saw miserable to restart in the tree or on the ground.
highlights: Replacement recoil pull handle
For Husqvarna 500 series saws
Fixes cracked or missing grips
Quick fix with no special tools

body.h: A small part that stops a crew
p: A broken starter handle sounds minor until the saw will not start at the end of the day. Handles get brittle with age and UV, and letting the cord snap back against the housing cracks them fast.
Keeping a spare in the truck box is cheap insurance, especially if your crew runs several 500 series saws.
Climbers who start a top-handle or ground saw in awkward positions are especially hard on handles, and a missing grip can mean pulling a thin cord with bare fingers, which is a good way to get hurt.

Remove the starter cover, release spring tension carefully, and pull the cord out. Thread it through the new handle, tie a firm stopper knot, and tuck the knot into the handle pocket. Re-tension the spring per the service manual so the handle sits snug against the housing with no slack.
If the handle keeps cracking, look at how the saw is being started. A steady, straight pull with the saw secured is easier on the handle, cord, and starter than a yank at an angle.

Check the starter cord while you are there; if it is frayed, replace it at the same time. Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. See all saw parts.

faq.q: Which saws are in the Husqvarna 500 series?
faq.a: The 500 series covers saws numbered in the 5xx range. Starter parts are not identical across every model, so check the part number against your saw.

faq.q: Should I replace the cord at the same time?
faq.a: If the cord is frayed, glazed, or short, yes. It takes little extra time once the starter is off.

name: Replacement Screw for Husqvarna 395XP Muffler
title: Husqvarna 395XP Muffler Screw Replacement
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 395XP muffler screw for a loose or lost muffler bolt. Why vibration loosens them, how to fit and check them, and the typical parts price.
tagline: Replacement muffler mounting screw for the Husqvarna 395XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP muffler screw replaces a lost, stripped, or stretched bolt that holds the muffler to the cylinder. A big saw vibrates hard, and a loose muffler can leak exhaust, crack its gasket, or damage the threads in the cylinder.
highlights: Replacement muffler mounting screw
For the Husqvarna 395XP
Fixes loose or missing muffler bolts
Cheap part that prevents expensive damage

p: The 395XP is a heavy, high-displacement saw that spends its day in big wood. Heat cycles and vibration work muffler screws loose over time, and once one backs out the others take the load and follow.
Running a saw with a loose muffler can leak hot exhaust where it should not, damage the gasket, and in the worst case strip the threads in the cylinder.
Missing screws also let the muffler shift, which can stress the exhaust gasket and the cylinder ports. It is a small part, but it protects some of the most expensive pieces of the saw.

Let the saw cool, clean the threads, and fit the new screw with the muffler gasket in place. Tighten evenly to the torque in the service manual rather than guessing. Check muffler screws as part of regular saw maintenance, along with the spark arrestor screen.
If a thread in the cylinder is already damaged, have a qualified shop repair it rather than forcing a new screw in at an angle.

Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. Browse other chainsaw parts for big saws.

faq.q: Can I use any bolt on my 395XP muffler?
faq.a: Use the correct part. Muffler screws need the right length, thread, and heat tolerance, and the wrong bolt can bottom out or work loose.

faq.q: How often should I check muffler screws?
faq.a: Check them during routine saw maintenance and any time you notice a rattle or exhaust leak.

name: Replacement Sprocket Nose for Husqvarna Light Bars
title: Husqvarna Bar Sprocket Nose Replacement for Light Bars
h1: Husqvarna Bar Sprocket Nose for Light Bars
meta: Husqvarna bar sprocket nose replacement for light bars with a worn or seized tip. Save a good bar body, signs the nose is done, and the typical street price.
tagline: Replaceable nose sprocket that brings a worn Husqvarna light bar back to life.
summary: This Husqvarna bar sprocket nose replaces the worn or seized tip on compatible Husqvarna light bars with a replaceable nose. If the bar rails are still straight and square but the nose sprocket is loose, notchy, or locked up, swapping the nose is cheaper than buying a new bar.
highlights: Replaceable sprocket nose for Husqvarna light bars
Saves a bar body with good rails
Restores smooth chain travel around the tip
Fixes seized or wobbly nose sprockets
specs: Husqvarna light bars with replaceable nose (check bar code)

p: The nose sprocket takes a beating, especially when you bore cut or work the tip in limbs. Signs it is finished include side-to-side play, a gritty or seized sprocket, chipped teeth, and chain that slows or jumps at the tip.
If the rails are worn, spread, or bent, a new nose will not fix the bar. Check the rails first and only rebuild a bar that is still straight.
Light bars save weight on a long bar, which matters when you are bucking or felling all day. Keeping a good bar body in service with a fresh nose makes that investment last longer.

Replaceable noses are held in with rivets that are drilled or ground out, then the new nose is riveted in place. Follow the manufacturer's instructions, and grease the nose sprocket through its grease hole if your bar has one. Match the nose to the bar's pitch and model code.
Dress the rails with a bar file after the swap so the chain sits square, and check that the chain still fits the nose sprocket cleanly before you go back to cutting.

Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. More bar and saw parts live in chainsaw parts.

faq.q: Can every Husqvarna bar take a replacement nose?
faq.a: No. Only bars built with a replaceable nose can be rebuilt this way, and the nose must match the bar model and chain pitch.

faq.q: Is it worth replacing a bar nose?
faq.a: It is worth it on a bar with straight, square rails. If the rails are worn out, buy a new bar instead.

name: Start/Stop Switch for Husqvarna 372XP
title: Husqvarna 372XP Stop Switch Replacement
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 372XP stop switch for a saw that won't shut off or won't start. How to diagnose a bad switch, fitting tips, and the typical parts price.
tagline: Replacement ignition stop switch for the Husqvarna 372XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 372XP stop switch replaces the start/stop control that grounds the ignition to kill the engine. A worn or broken switch can leave the saw unable to start or, worse, unable to shut off, and that needs fixing before the saw goes back to work.
highlights: Replacement start/stop switch for the 372XP
Restores reliable engine shut-off
Fixes no-start problems caused by a stuck switch
Shop repair with basic tools

p: On the 372XP the stop switch grounds the ignition module. If the switch sticks in the stop position, the saw will crank without firing. If the switch or its wire is broken, the saw may keep running when you flip it to stop, which means shutting it off with the choke and taking it out of service.
Before you replace the switch, check the kill wire for chafing or a loose connection under the top cover.
A reliable stop switch is a basic safety control. If you cannot kill the saw instantly, you cannot react safely when something goes wrong in the cut.

Remove the top cover and air filter area as described in the service manual, disconnect the old switch, and fit the new one so it moves cleanly between run and stop. Test that the saw stops every time before it goes back on the truck.

Keep the area around the switch clean, since packed sawdust and resin can stop it from moving fully into the stop position. Check its function as part of your daily saw inspection along with the chain brake and throttle lockout.
Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. See more Husqvarna parts.

faq.q: My 372XP won't shut off. Is it the switch?
faq.a: Often it is the switch or a broken ground wire. Do not use the saw until it shuts off reliably with the stop control.

faq.q: Can a stop switch cause a no-start?
faq.a: Yes. A switch stuck in the stop position or a shorted wire grounds the ignition and prevents a spark.

name: Starter Cord for Husqvarna 395XP Chainsaw
title: Husqvarna 395XP Starter Cord Replacement
meta: Replacement Husqvarna 395XP starter cord for a frayed or snapped pull rope. Why big-saw cords wear out, tips for fitting and tensioning, and typical price.
tagline: Replacement recoil starter rope for the Husqvarna 395XP.
summary: This Husqvarna 395XP starter cord replaces the recoil rope on one of the biggest saws in a tree crew's lineup. A high-compression saw puts real load on the cord, and a frayed rope tends to snap at the worst time.
highlights: Replacement recoil starter cord
For the Husqvarna 395XP
Fixes frayed, glazed, or broken ropes
Good spare to keep in the truck

p: Starting a 90cc-class saw takes a firm pull, and every pull rubs the cord on the starter housing and handle. Pulling at an angle, letting the handle snap back, and working in grit all speed up wear.
Look for fuzzing, flat spots, or a cord that has been knotted short. Replace it before it breaks.
A spare starter cord rolled up in the truck box weighs nothing and can save a trip back to the shop when a cord snaps mid-job.

Remove the starter assembly, release the spring tension, and pull the old cord out. Feed the new cord through the pulley and handle, tie it off, and wind the pulley to preload the spring per the service manual so the handle returns snug without bottoming out the spring.
Pull the cord out fully once the starter is back together to confirm the spring has enough reserve, then let it retract slowly to check that the handle seats properly.

Fit a new handle too if the old one is cracked. Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. More 395XP parts are listed here.

faq.q: Can I use generic starter rope on a 395XP?
faq.a: Use rope of the correct diameter and length for the saw. Too thick a rope will not wind fully, and too thin wears out fast.

faq.q: How tight should the starter spring be?
faq.a: Follow the service manual. The handle should sit snug against the housing, and the pulley should still turn a little further when the cord is fully pulled out.

name: Starter Pawl and Spring Kit for Husqvarna 550XP Mark II
title: Husqvarna 550XP Starter Pawl & Spring Kit (Mark II)
h1: Husqvarna 550XP Starter Pawl and Spring Kit (Mark II)
meta: Husqvarna 550XP starter pawl and spring kit for the Mark II. Fix a starter that pulls but doesn't turn the engine over, with fitting tips and typical price.
tagline: Replacement flywheel pawls and springs for the 550XP Mark II starter.
summary: This Husqvarna 550XP starter pawl and spring kit for the Mark II replaces the small spring-loaded pawls that catch the starter pulley and turn the engine. When pawls wear or springs weaken, the cord pulls freely without cranking the saw.
highlights: Pawls and springs for the 550XP Mark II
Fixes a starter that slips without cranking
Restores positive engagement on the pull
Inexpensive fix with basic tools

p: When you pull the starter cord, the pulley catches spring-loaded pawls on the flywheel and spins the engine. Once the saw fires, the pawls fling out of the way. Over time the pawl tips round over and the springs weaken, so the pulley slips or engages only some of the time.
If your 550XP Mark II starter pulls with no resistance and the engine does not turn, look here first.
Cold weather and old, gummy grease can make pawls stick, so cleaning the flywheel area is part of the fix. Sawdust packed around the pawls also blocks the cooling air the engine needs.

Remove the starter cover to expose the flywheel, clean out sawdust and grime, and replace the pawls and springs as a set. Make sure each pawl pivots freely and snaps back. A clean flywheel area also keeps the cooling fins working.
Inspect the starter pulley teeth that the pawls catch on. If they are rounded or chipped, replace the pulley at the same time so the new pawls have something solid to grab.

Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. See more 550XP parts in the parts section.

faq.q: Why does my starter cord pull freely without turning the engine?
faq.a: Worn pawls or weak pawl springs are a common cause. A damaged starter pulley can do the same.

faq.q: Should I replace both pawls?
faq.a: Yes. Replacing them as a set keeps engagement even and avoids a second teardown.

name: Starter Pawl for Husqvarna Chainsaws
title: Husqvarna Starter Pawl: Replacement Flywheel Pawl
meta: Replacement Husqvarna starter pawl for chainsaws whose starter slips without cranking the engine. How to diagnose wear, fit the pawl, and typical price.
tagline: Replacement flywheel pawl for Husqvarna chainsaw recoil starters.
summary: This Husqvarna starter pawl is the small catch on the flywheel that the recoil starter grabs to turn the engine. A worn or broken pawl lets the starter slip, so the cord pulls but the saw never cranks.
highlights: Replacement starter pawl
For Husqvarna chainsaws (check fit)
Fixes slipping recoil starters
Cheap part, quick repair
specs: Husqvarna chainsaws (confirm part number for your model)

p: Pull the starter cover and look at the flywheel. Pawls should pivot freely and spring back. Rounded tips, cracked pawls, or missing springs all lead to a starter that grabs only sometimes or not at all.
Also check the starter pulley's engagement teeth; if they are chewed up, replace the pulley along with the pawl.
A starter that only catches every few pulls is often the first sign, long before it fails completely. Fixing it early saves time and frustration on the job.

Clean the flywheel area, swap the pawl and spring, and confirm smooth movement before refitting the cover. Avoid yanking the cord at an angle and keep the starter area free of packed sawdust to make the new pawl last.

Check the pawl spring as well as the pawl. A weak spring lets the pawl stay retracted, which feels the same as a worn pawl from the starter handle. Replace both if in doubt, and test the starter several times before reassembling the rest of the saw.

Confirm the part number against your saw's model and serial plate or the manufacturer's parts lookup before ordering, since parts can change between production runs. Browse more Husqvarna chainsaw parts.

faq.q: Does one pawl fit all Husqvarna saws?
faq.a: No. Pawls vary by model and flywheel, so match the part number to your saw.

faq.q: Do I need to remove the flywheel?
faq.a: On many saws the pawls can be serviced with the starter cover off. Check the service manual for your model.

name: 1100 Series Compatible Stump Grinder Teeth
title: 1100 Series Stump Grinder Teeth (Compatible)
meta: 1100 series stump grinder teeth made to fit grinders running 1100-style pockets. How to tell when teeth are worn, rotation tips and typical per-tooth price.
tagline: Replacement carbide teeth for stump grinders set up with 1100-series pockets.
summary: These 1100 series stump grinder teeth are compatible replacement teeth for cutter wheels running 1100-style tooth pockets. Sharp carbide keeps a grinder chewing instead of rubbing, which saves fuel, belts, and time on every stump.
highlights: Compatible with 1100-series tooth pockets
Carbide-tipped cutting teeth
Restore cutting speed on worn wheels
Replace singly or as a full set

p: Dull teeth show up as more smoke than chips, a grinder that bogs, and fine dust instead of coarse chips. Look for rounded or chipped carbide and teeth worn down into the shank. Rocks and buried metal can knock off a tip in one pass.
Many 1100-style teeth can be rotated to bring a fresh edge into the cut before you replace them, which stretches the life of a set.
Running teeth until they wear into the shank damages pockets and costs more in the long run. Watching the chip size is the simplest way to know when to rotate or swap.

Match the tooth to the pocket system on your wheel and torque the nuts to the wheel maker's spec. Replace worn bolts and pockets as needed so the new teeth sit tight. Wear eye and face protection, and lock out the machine before working on the wheel.

Keep a spare set of teeth, bolts, and the right sockets in the grinder truck so a broken tip on a rock does not end the day. Check torque again after the first stump with fresh teeth, since new hardware can settle in.
Compatible teeth are an affordable way to keep a wheel cutting. See the full range of stump grinding parts.

faq.q: Will 1100 series teeth fit my grinder?
faq.a: They fit wheels set up with 1100-series pockets. Check your current pockets and teeth before ordering.

faq.q: Should I replace all the teeth at once?
faq.a: Replacing a full set keeps the wheel balanced and cutting evenly, but swapping a few damaged teeth is fine on a mostly sharp wheel.

name: 700 Series Compatible Stump Grinder Teeth
title: 700 Series Stump Grinder Teeth (Compatible)
meta: 700 series stump grinder teeth that fit wheels with 700-style pockets. Signs your teeth are dull, tips for fitting and rotating, and the typical tooth price.
tagline: Replacement carbide teeth for grinders set up with 700-series pockets.
summary: These 700 series stump grinder teeth are compatible replacements for cutter wheels using 700-style tooth pockets. Fresh carbide keeps a small or mid-size grinder cutting cleanly instead of bouncing off the stump.
highlights: Compatible with 700-series tooth pockets
Carbide-tipped cutting teeth
Brings back cutting speed
Good stock item for rental and crew grinders

p: Stump grinding is hard on teeth. Dirt, sand, and hidden rocks wear carbide quickly, and a wheel with a few broken tips cuts unevenly and vibrates. When you see more dust than chips or the machine starts bogging, inspect every tooth.
Replace teeth with chipped or missing carbide, and rotate teeth that can be turned to a fresh edge.
Rental and smaller self-propelled grinders often use 700-style systems, so these are common stock items for crews that grind lots of small stumps.

On sandy or rocky sites, expect teeth to wear much faster than on clean loam. Raking back dirt and checking for rocks before you start, and grinding in controlled sweeps rather than plunging deep, both help a set of teeth last longer.

Shut down and lock out the grinder before touching the wheel. Clean the pockets, fit the teeth in the correct orientation, and torque the hardware to spec. Check bolts and pockets for wear while you are there; a loose tooth can damage the wheel.

Keep a written record of when teeth were changed and how many stumps the set has done. It makes it easier to spot when a wheel is wearing unusually fast, which can point to rocky sites or loose hardware.
Wear eye and face protection when grinding and keep bystanders well back. More stump grinder teeth and parts are in this section.

faq.q: What does 700 series mean?
faq.a: It refers to the tooth and pocket system on the cutter wheel. Teeth only fit pockets made for that system.

faq.q: Can I sharpen stump grinder teeth?
faq.a: Carbide teeth can sometimes be touched up with a diamond wheel, but most crews rotate or replace them.

name: Green Teeth 900 Series Spacer
title: Green Teeth 900 Series Spacer for Stump Grinders
meta: Green Teeth 900 series spacer for stump grinder cutter wheels. What spacers do in a Green Teeth setup, when to replace them, and the typical parts price.
tagline: Replacement spacer for Green Teeth 900-series cutter wheel setups.
summary: This Green Teeth 900 series spacer is part of the hardware that positions teeth and pockets on a stump grinder cutter wheel. Worn or missing spacers let teeth sit out of position, which costs cutting performance and can loosen hardware.
highlights: Spacer for Green Teeth 900 series
Keeps teeth and pockets correctly positioned
Replace worn hardware during a tooth change
Small part that protects the wheel

p: On a Green Teeth wheel, spacers help set the position of the pockets and teeth so they cut in the intended pattern. If a spacer wears, cracks, or is left out, the tooth can sit off line, take extra load, and loosen in use.
When you replace teeth, look at every spacer and pocket. Hardware wear is easy to miss until a tooth comes loose.
A spacer costs little compared with a damaged pocket or a cutter wheel that has been chewed up by a loose tooth, so it is worth replacing worn ones at every tooth change.

Lock out the machine and clean the wheel before you start. Follow the wheel layout chart for your grinder so spacers go back in the right positions, and torque the bolts to spec. Use new bolts if threads are damaged.

Lay the old hardware out in order as it comes off so the new teeth, pockets, and spacers go back in the right places. Keep a few spares in the toolbox so a missing spacer never holds up the job, and recheck bolt torque after the first stump.
Wear eye and face protection and keep bystanders clear when grinding. See more stump grinding parts.

faq.q: Do I need spacers on every pocket?
faq.a: It depends on the wheel layout. Follow the layout chart for your grinder model.

faq.q: Will this fit other tooth systems?
faq.a: It is made for the 900 series. Check your system before ordering.

name: Lo-Pro Stump Grinder Bolt
title: Lo-Pro Stump Grinder Bolt for Tooth Pockets
meta: Lo-Pro stump grinder bolt for securing teeth and pockets on cutter wheels. Why worn tooth bolts cause trouble, when to replace them and the typical price.
tagline: Replacement bolt for low-profile stump grinder tooth systems.
summary: This Lo-Pro stump grinder bolt is a replacement tooth bolt for low-profile tooth and pocket setups. Bolts stretch, round off, and get beaten by rocks, and a bad bolt is the usual reason a tooth comes loose.
highlights: Replacement bolt for Lo-Pro tooth setups
Holds teeth and pockets tight to the wheel
Replace damaged bolts during tooth changes
Keep spares in the grinder toolbox

p: Teeth take hard impacts on every revolution of the cutter wheel. The bolt holding a tooth and pocket does a lot of work, and it wears with the teeth. Rounded heads, damaged threads, and bolts that have been over-torqued are all reasons to replace.
A loose tooth throws the wheel out of balance and can damage pockets and the wheel itself.
Lo-Pro and other low-profile systems put the tooth close to the wheel, so bolt condition and correct length matter to keep teeth seated and to avoid hardware sticking out where it can catch.

Lock out the grinder and clean the wheel. Match the bolt to your tooth system and wheel thickness, use new nuts where required, and torque to the spec for your system. Recheck torque after the first stump.

Keep spare bolts with the teeth and a calibrated torque wrench in the truck. A tooth change is the right time to replace any questionable bolts rather than waiting for one to fail on the next job. Use anti-seize only if your tooth system's instructions allow it.
Grinding throws debris, so wear eye and face protection and keep bystanders back. Browse more stump grinding hardware.

faq.q: How often should I replace tooth bolts?
faq.a: Inspect them at every tooth change and replace any that are stretched, bent, or damaged.

faq.q: Can I reuse the nut?
faq.a: Follow your tooth system's guidance. Locking nuts lose their hold after repeated use.

name: Pocket for Standard Stump Grinder Teeth
title: Stump Grinder Tooth Pocket for Standard Teeth
h1: Stump Grinder Tooth Pocket for Standard Teeth
meta: Replacement stump grinder tooth pocket for standard teeth. How worn pockets loosen teeth, when to swap them during a tooth change, and the typical price.
tagline: Replacement pocket that holds standard teeth on a stump grinder wheel.
summary: This stump grinder tooth pocket holds a standard tooth on the cutter wheel. Pockets take the same punishment as the teeth, and a worn pocket lets even a new tooth shift and loosen.
highlights: Pocket for standard stump grinder teeth
Seats teeth firmly on the wheel
Replace worn or cracked pockets
Pairs with new teeth and bolts

p: The pocket clamps the tooth to the cutter wheel and supports it against impact. When a pocket wears, cracks, or gets peened by rocks, the tooth no longer seats tightly. You will see teeth working loose, uneven cutting, and more vibration.
Check pockets at every tooth change, especially after hitting rock or buried metal.
Pockets can also wear on the face where the tooth seats. Even if the pocket looks whole, a tooth that will not tighten down square is a sign the pocket is done.
Rocky sites, buried concrete, and old fence posts are hard on pockets. Probing around a stump and raking back loose stones before grinding helps protect both pockets and teeth.
Lock out the grinder and clean the wheel. Fit the pocket in the correct orientation for the wheel's rotation, use good bolts and nuts, and torque to spec. Recheck after a short run.

Change pockets in pairs or sets where your wheel layout calls for it, so the wheel stays balanced. Keep a spare pocket, bolts, and teeth in the grinder truck. A wheel that runs smooth and true cuts faster and is easier on bearings, belts, and the operator.
Wear eye and face protection when grinding. Find teeth, bolts, and more stump grinding parts in this section.

faq.q: Do I need to replace pockets with teeth?
faq.a: Not every time, but replace any pocket that is cracked, worn, or no longer holds a tooth tight.

faq.q: Will this fit my wheel?
faq.a: It fits wheels set up for standard teeth. Compare it with your current pockets before ordering.

name: TreeHog Mesh Stump Grinding Guard System
title: TreeHog Mesh Stump Grinder Guard System
h1: TreeHog Mesh Stump Grinder Guard System
meta: TreeHog mesh stump grinder guard system for containing chips and debris around the grinding area. How it fits into a safe setup on residential jobs, and price.
tagline: Portable mesh screens that help contain debris thrown by a stump grinder.
summary: The TreeHog mesh stump grinding guard system is a portable stump grinder guard that sets up around the work area to help catch chips, stones, and debris thrown by the cutter wheel. It is useful on tight residential jobs near windows, cars, and walkways.
highlights: Portable mesh screen guard system
Helps contain chips and thrown debris
Useful near houses, cars, and walkways
Sets up around the grinding area

p: A stump grinder throws chips hard and can launch stones and buried debris. On a back-yard job next to a patio door or a parked car, the machine's own guard is not always enough. A portable mesh screen around the work zone adds another layer between the cutter wheel and whatever needs protecting.
Mesh lets the operator see the stump and surroundings while still catching much of the debris.
Clients notice when their siding, windows, and cars come through a stump job without a scratch. A guard system also saves cleanup time by keeping more chips in one place.

Set the screens up before you start, positioned on the side where debris would cause damage or injury. A guard does not replace a proper exclusion zone: keep bystanders and pets well back, call underground utilities before you grind, and wear eye, face, and hearing protection.
Inspect the mesh and frames for tears or bent parts before each job and repair or replace damaged panels. A torn screen will not stop the debris you are relying on it to catch.
Follow the manufacturer's setup instructions. Browse more stump grinding gear for your grinder.

faq.q: Do I still need an exclusion zone with a guard?
faq.a: Yes. A guard reduces thrown debris but does not remove the need to keep people clear of the work area.

faq.q: Does it fit any grinder?
faq.a: It is a freestanding screen system set up around the work area rather than a part bolted to one machine. Check the manufacturer's details for setup.

name: Husqvarna 4-Gallon Backpack Sprayer
title: Husqvarna Backpack Sprayer, 4 Gallon: Uses & Care
meta: The Husqvarna backpack sprayer holds 4 gallons for spot spraying, stump treatment and plant health work. How crews use it, care tips and typical street price.
tagline: 4-gallon manual backpack sprayer for spot treatments and plant health work.
summary: The Husqvarna backpack sprayer carries 4 gallons on your back for spot spraying, cut-stump treatments, and plant health applications. A pump handle builds pressure as you walk, so both hands stay free to aim the wand.
highlights: 4-gallon tank carried as a backpack
Manual pump for steady pressure
Wand for directed spot spraying
Good for cut-stump and plant health work

body.h: Where it fits in tree work
p: Tree crews use a backpack sprayer for cut-stump herbicide on brush clearing jobs, spot spraying around plantings, and plant health treatments that need more volume than a handheld bottle. Four gallons covers a good stretch of right-of-way or a large property without constant refills.
Carrying the load on your back keeps you mobile on slopes and in brush where a cart sprayer will not go.
A good backpack sprayer also helps with vegetation control around storm cleanup sites, along fence lines, and in nursery work where crews need to cover ground on foot.

Follow the label on any product you apply; the label is the law, and many products require a license. Wear the PPE the label calls for. Flush the tank, pump, and wand with clean water after each use, and keep separate sprayers for herbicides and other products.

Release pressure before opening the tank, and store the sprayer empty and clean with the pump handle secured. Replace worn gaskets and nozzles early, since a leaking sprayer can put product on your back and legs.
Check seals and the wand shutoff before each job. More landscaper tools are in this section.

faq.q: Can I use one sprayer for herbicide and fertilizer?
faq.a: It is safer to keep a dedicated herbicide sprayer, since residue can damage plants even after rinsing.

faq.q: How do I clean a backpack sprayer?
faq.a: Rinse the tank, pump, and wand with clean water, spray it through, and dispose of rinse water as the product label directs.

name: Husqvarna 48 oz Handheld Sprayer
title: Husqvarna Handheld Sprayer, 48 oz
meta: The Husqvarna handheld sprayer holds 48 oz for small spot treatments, wound care and cut-stump work. How tree crews use it, care tips and typical price.
tagline: Compact 48 oz pump sprayer for small spot treatments.
summary: The Husqvarna handheld sprayer is a compact 48 oz pump bottle for small jobs: a few cut stumps, spot treatments around plantings, or a quick application that does not justify filling a backpack sprayer.
highlights: 48 oz capacity
Hand pump builds pressure
Adjustable spray from stream to mist
Easy to stash in the truck

p: A handheld sprayer is handy when you only need a little product. Treat a handful of fresh stumps after removals, spot spray around a new planting, or apply a product at a client's property without hauling a 4-gallon tank.
It also works with plain water for cleaning tools and wetting down dust on small jobs.
It is light enough to carry in one hand while you work through a site with a hand saw or loppers in the other.

Read and follow the product label, which may require specific PPE or a license. Label the sprayer for its product and do not mix uses. Rinse it out after use and store it out of direct sun so the plastic and seals last.

Release pressure before removing the top and never leave a pressurized sprayer in a hot truck cab. Keep it upright when stored so product does not leak around the seals. A cheap handheld sprayer is easy to dedicate to one product, which is the simplest way to avoid cross-contamination. Write the product name on the bottle with a marker.
For bigger jobs, step up to a backpack sprayer. Find more landscaper tools here.

faq.q: Is a handheld sprayer enough for cut-stump treatment?
faq.a: For a few stumps, yes. For larger clearing jobs, a backpack sprayer saves refilling time.

faq.q: How do I keep the nozzle from clogging?
faq.a: Mix products fully, rinse after each use, and do not leave product sitting in the sprayer.

name: Husqvarna Blue EHS Metal Blade 14 in
title: Husqvarna Metal Blade, 14 Inch (Blue EHS)
meta: Husqvarna metal blade, 14 inch, in the blue EHS finish. A replacement cutting blade for compatible Husqvarna tools, with fitting notes and typical price.
tagline: 14-inch replacement metal blade for compatible Husqvarna tools.
summary: This Husqvarna metal blade is a 14-inch replacement blade in the blue EHS finish for compatible Husqvarna equipment. Check your tool's manual for the approved blade, arbor size, and guard before fitting it.
highlights: 14-inch metal blade
Husqvarna replacement part
Blue finish for easy identification
Fit only to tools approved for this blade

body.h: Matching the blade to the tool
p: Blades are not universal. The arbor size, rated speed, and guard on your machine all need to match the blade, and only blades listed in the operator's manual should go on a given tool. If you are unsure, compare the part number on your old blade with the parts list for your machine.
Fitting the wrong blade can overload the tool or leave the blade unguarded.
The blue EHS finish makes the blade easy to spot in a truck box or shop shelf, which helps keep it with the right machine. If you run several Husqvarna tools, label blades by machine.
Keep the old blade until the new one is fitted and checked, so you can compare diameter, arbor hole, and tooth pattern side by side. Any mismatch is a reason to stop and confirm the part.

Always fit the correct guard, tighten the blade fastener as the manual specifies, and inspect the blade for cracks, bends, or missing teeth before each use. Replace a damaged blade rather than straightening it.
Store spare blades flat and dry, with the cutting edge covered, so the teeth stay sharp and no one grabs an exposed edge.
Wear eye, face, hearing, and leg protection as the manual directs, and keep bystanders clear. More landscaper tools are in this section.

faq.q: Will this blade fit my Husqvarna tool?
faq.a: Only if your operator's manual lists it as approved. Check arbor size, rated speed, and guard requirements.

faq.q: When should I replace a metal blade?
faq.a: Replace it if it is cracked, bent, out of balance, or has damaged teeth.

name: Husqvarna Felling Bar with Cant Hook
title: Husqvarna Felling Bar with Cant Hook
h1: Husqvarna Felling Bar with Cant Hook
meta: The Husqvarna felling bar with cant hook helps push over trees and roll logs. How it works when felling and bucking, what to watch for, and typical price.
tagline: Steel felling lever with a turning hook for felling help and rolling logs.
summary: The Husqvarna felling bar with cant hook is a steel lever that helps tip small and mid-size trees in the direction of the notch and then doubles as a cant hook for rolling logs while you buck. It is a staple tool for ground crews and firewood cutters.
highlights: Felling lever with built-in turning hook
Helps push trees over the hinge
Rolls logs for bucking
Lifts logs off the ground to protect the chain

p: After the notch and back cut are set, the blade of the felling bar goes into the back cut and you lever the tree over the hinge. It is useful on trees that sit back or lean slightly, and it keeps you standing at the stump instead of pounding wedges in a hurry.
It has limits. A tree with a real back lean needs wedges, a pull line, or a different plan, and a lever is no substitute for a proper felling cut.
On firewood and storm cleanup jobs, it saves your back. Rolling logs with a hook instead of lifting them reduces strain over a full day.

Flip the bar and the hook grabs a log to roll it, so you can finish a cut without putting the chain in the dirt. You can also lever a log up onto a scrap piece to keep it off the ground while bucking.
Check the blade and hook for bends or cracks before use. A bent felling bar does not seat properly in the back cut and can slip under load.
Keep a firm stance and clear footing, and wear chaps and boots. Find more ground tools for the crew.

faq.q: Can a felling bar replace wedges?
faq.a: Not entirely. It helps on trees with little or no back lean, but wedges or a pull line are needed for heavier or back-leaning trees.

faq.q: What size trees is it good for?
faq.a: It suits small to mid-size trees. Larger trees need wedges or mechanical help.

name: Jameson Non-Conductive Soil Probe, 48 in
title: Jameson Soil Probe, Non-Conductive, 48 Inch
meta: The Jameson soil probe is a 48 inch non-conductive probe for checking soil, roots and buried obstructions. How tree crews use it, safety notes and price.
tagline: 48-inch non-conductive probe for checking soil and buried obstructions.
summary: The Jameson soil probe is a 48-inch non-conductive probe for pushing into the ground to check soil conditions, compaction, and buried obstructions before you dig, plant, or set equipment. Its non-conductive shaft adds a margin of safety when working near buried utilities.
highlights: 48-inch probe length
Non-conductive construction
Checks soil compaction and moisture
Helps locate rocks and roots before digging

p: A soil probe tells you a lot quickly. Push it in around a planting site to feel for compaction layers, rock, or old foundations. Use it to check soil moisture around a stressed tree, or to find the edges of a root plate before you set outriggers or a stump grinder.
Plant health care techs use it to judge where soil treatments or aeration will do the most good.
Arborists assessing a tree before construction or root work use a probe to estimate how much soil disturbance a site has seen. Hard, compacted layers often explain poor root growth and decline.
The 48-inch length lets you probe deeper than a short hand probe without kneeling, and gives you better leverage in firm soil. Take readings in several spots around a tree rather than relying on one.

A non-conductive probe reduces electrical risk, but it does not make probing near buried lines safe on its own. Call 811 and have utilities located before you dig or probe, keep to marked tolerance zones, and probe gently rather than driving the shaft.
Store it where the tip will not be damaged and keep the shaft clean so you can feel resistance clearly.
Clean the probe after use and check for cracks in the shaft. See more landscaper tools.

faq.q: Is a non-conductive probe safe near buried power lines?
faq.a: It lowers the risk but is not a substitute for having utilities located and marked before you work.

faq.q: What can a soil probe tell me?
faq.a: It helps you feel compaction, moisture, rock, and buried obstructions so you can plan planting, digging, or equipment placement.

name: Jameson Ram's Horn Nylon Twin-Prong Vine Puller and Lifter
title: Jameson Ram's Horn Vine Puller and Lifter
h1: Jameson Ram's Horn Vine Puller and Lifter, Twin-Prong
meta: The Jameson Ram's Horn vine puller is a nylon twin-prong pole head for pulling vines, lifting lines and clearing hangers from the ground. Uses, tips and price.
tagline: Nylon twin-prong pole head for pulling vines and lifting lines from the ground.
summary: The Jameson Ram's Horn vine puller is a nylon twin-prong head that mounts on a pole to pull vines, drag down small hangers, and lift or guide lines from the ground. It lets you clear material overhead without climbing for every small task.
highlights: Twin-prong hook head
Nylon construction
Mounts on a compatible pole
Pulls vines and small hangers
Lifts and guides ropes from the ground

p: Vines wrapped through a canopy and small broken limbs hung up in a crown are slow work to clear by climbing. With the Ram's Horn on a pole, you can hook the vine or hanger from the ground and pull it free. The twin prongs grab better than a single hook and are easier to release.
It is also handy for lifting a rope over a limb, repositioning a line, or retrieving a throw line from the ground.
Nylon is lighter than steel and less likely to scar bark when you hook a limb, which matters on high-value trees and client landscapes.

Stand clear of the drop zone when pulling anything down and wear a helmet and eye protection. Keep poles well away from overhead power lines; only qualified line-clearance workers with properly rated insulated tools should work near energized conductors.
Pull with steady force rather than jerking, and let the material come down before stepping in to clear it. Check the prongs for cracks or wear before each use, and replace the head if it is damaged.
Check that the head is secure on the pole before each use. More pole tools and landscaper tools are here.

faq.q: Does the Ram's Horn come with a pole?
faq.a: It is a pole head. Check the listing for what is included and make sure it fits your poles.

faq.q: Is a nylon head safe near power lines?
faq.a: No tool makes it safe for an unqualified worker. Stay well clear of energized lines unless you are trained and authorized.

name: CAMP Gyro Lanyard Single
title: CAMP Gyro Lanyard Single: Swivel Lanyard Guide
meta: The CAMP Gyro Lanyard Single is a sewn lanyard with a swivel at the harness end to stop twisting. How it works for climbers, inspection notes and typical price.
tagline: Single-leg sewn lanyard with a swivel connection to reduce twisting.
summary: The CAMP Gyro Lanyard Single is a single-leg sewn lanyard built around a swivel connection that lets it rotate instead of twisting as you move. It suits climbers and rope access workers who want a short, tidy tether that hangs clean from the harness.
highlights: Single-leg sewn lanyard
Swivel connection reduces twisting
Keeps the tether tidy at the harness
Pairs with a locking connector

p: A sewn lanyard that is clipped and unclipped all day tends to twist up, especially as you turn around a stem or move between anchors. The Gyro design puts a swivel in the system so the lanyard can rotate freely and lie flat.
That keeps the connector oriented correctly and makes clipping faster when you are reaching for an anchor.
Because the swivel lets the lanyard lie flat, it is easier to inspect too. Twisted webbing hides cuts and abrasion that you would otherwise see at a glance.
The single-leg version is a good choice for climbers who already carry a flipline or adjustable lanyard for positioning and want a simple, short tether for clipping in at a stance.

A single-leg lanyard is simple and light. If you need to stay connected while passing anchors, look at the twin version. Use only locking connectors that the manufacturer approves and that suit your harness attachment point, and check the length suits your work.
Store it clean and dry, out of direct sun, away from fuel and bar oil, and log its age and inspections the way you would any other life-support item.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. See all lanyard kits.

faq.q: Is the Gyro Lanyard a work-positioning lanyard?
faq.a: Check the manufacturer's instructions for the intended uses and standards before using it for positioning or fall restraint.

faq.q: Single or twin?
faq.a: Single is lighter and simpler. Twin lets you clip the next anchor before you unclip the last.

name: CAMP Gyro Lanyard Twin
title: CAMP Gyro Lanyard Twin: Y-Lanyard with Swivel
meta: The CAMP Gyro Lanyard Twin is a two-leg sewn lanyard with a swivel to stop twisting, letting you clip a new anchor before leaving the last. Uses and price.
tagline: Two-leg sewn lanyard with a swivel for continuous connection.
summary: The CAMP Gyro Lanyard Twin is a two-leg sewn lanyard with a swivel connection that keeps both legs from twisting together. Two legs let you clip the next anchor before you unclip the last, so you stay connected while moving.
highlights: Two-leg (Y) sewn lanyard
Swivel reduces twisting between legs
Lets you stay connected while passing anchors
Clean, tidy hang at the harness

p: Twin lanyards are great until the legs wind around each other. The Gyro's swivel lets the system rotate as you move, so the legs hang separately and each one is ready to clip.
On a tree or structure where you pass limbs, crotches, or anchor points, the second leg lets you clip ahead before releasing behind you.
It suits climbers and work-at-height crews who spend time moving between anchors, and it pairs well with a flipline or adjustable lanyard for positioning at the work.

Fit locking connectors approved by the manufacturer on each leg, and attach the lanyard to the harness point its instructions specify. Unused legs should be stowed where the manufacturer recommends, not clipped to a random gear loop.

Inspect both legs, the sewing, and the swivel before every use. Retire the lanyard after a fall or any sign of damage, and keep a record of its age and inspections. A twisted or snagged leg should be cleared before it is relied on.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Compare more lanyard kits.

faq.q: What is a twin lanyard for?
faq.a: It lets you stay connected while moving between anchors by clipping one leg ahead before unclipping the other.

faq.q: Can I use it for fall arrest?
faq.a: Only as the manufacturer's instructions allow. Check the certifications and intended use before relying on it.

name: DMM Nomad Lanyard (ZUU7)
title: DMM Nomad Lanyard (ZUU7) Adjustable Lanyard
meta: The DMM Nomad lanyard, listed as ZUU7, is an adjustable lanyard for work at height. What sets it apart, how to check the model code, and typical price.
tagline: Adjustable DMM lanyard for positioning and work at height, ZUU7 version.
summary: This DMM Nomad lanyard listing covers the ZUU7 version, an adjustable lanyard that lets you change your tether length at the harness. Adjustable length means you can sit back into a position or snug up close to the work without re-rigging.
highlights: Adjustable-length lanyard
ZUU7 model listing
Fine-tune your position at the work
DMM build quality and connectors

p: A fixed lanyard is the right length only some of the time. With an adjustable lanyard like the Nomad, you can let out length to reach and shorten it to lean back and work with both hands. Fine adjustments add up to less fatigue over a long day.
The ZUU7 code identifies a specific Nomad configuration. Compare it with DMM's current product codes to confirm length and connector options before ordering.
If you already run a Nomad, keep track of which version you own so replacement parts and accessories match.

Follow DMM's instructions for attachment points, connector orientation, and intended use. Learn how the adjuster behaves under load low to the ground before relying on it at height, and keep the lanyard away from saw cuts and sharp edges.

Inspect the adjuster, rope, and terminations before every climb. Retire the lanyard if the sheath is cut, the core is exposed, or the adjuster shows grooves, cracks, or sticky movement. Store it clean, dry, and out of the sun and away from fuel and bar oil.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. See more lanyard kits.

faq.q: What does ZUU7 mean?
faq.a: It appears to be a model or product code for one Nomad configuration. Check DMM's product listings for the exact length and connectors it includes.

faq.q: Is the Nomad suitable for tree work?
faq.a: Check DMM's instructions and certifications for the intended use, and confirm it suits your employer's and ANSI Z133 requirements.

name: DMM Nomad Lanyard
title: DMM Nomad Lanyard: Adjustable Work Lanyard
meta: The DMM Nomad lanyard is an adjustable lanyard for positioning at height. How the adjuster helps on the job, setup and inspection notes, and typical price.
tagline: Adjustable DMM lanyard for setting your position at height.
summary: The DMM Nomad lanyard is an adjustable lanyard that lets you shorten or extend your tether at the harness to get into the right working position. It is built for climbers and work-at-height crews who adjust their reach all day.
highlights: Adjustable-length lanyard
Quick length changes at the harness
Helps you work hands-free in position
DMM design and hardware

p: Positioning is half the work at height. With a fixed lanyard you either reach too far or hang too close. The Nomad's adjuster lets you set the distance that keeps your body balanced and your hands free for the saw or the rigging.
Small changes as you move around a stem or structure save energy and keep you working in a stable stance.
An adjustable lanyard also makes it easier to pair with your main climbing system, since you can set it to share load with your climbing line in a comfortable working position.

Attach the lanyard only to the harness points DMM specifies and use approved locking connectors. Practice adjustment low to the ground. Inspect the rope, sewing, adjuster, and connectors before every use and retire anything cut, glazed, or contaminated.
Store it clean, dry, and out of direct sun, away from fuel and bar oil, and keep a record of its age and inspections the way you would for any life-support item. Retire it after a fall or any damage.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Compare other lanyard kits.

faq.q: Can I use the Nomad as a flipline?
faq.a: Check DMM's instructions for intended uses. Steel-core fliplines are often preferred when cutting near the lanyard.

faq.q: How long does the Nomad adjust?
faq.a: Length depends on the version. Check the product listing for the specific configuration.

name: LogRite BTS Hauler with Wide Tires
title: LogRite BTS Hauler with Wide Tires: Log Arch Guide
h1: LogRite BTS Hauler with Wide Tires
meta: The LogRite BTS hauler with wide tires lifts one end of a log so you can roll it out by hand instead of dragging it. How crews use it, tips and typical price.
tagline: Log arch with wide tires for moving logs out of yards and woods.
summary: The LogRite BTS hauler rides on wide tires and lifts the end of a log off the ground so you can move it out with less effort and less ground damage. It is a practical tool for crews working in back yards where a loader cannot reach.
highlights: Log arch that lifts one end of the log
Wide tires for soft ground and lawns
Moves logs where machines can't reach
Reduces dragging damage to turf

p: On a back-yard removal, the trunk wood is often the hardest part to get to the street. A log arch hooks the end of a log, lifts it as you lever the handle down, and rolls it out on its wheels. Wide tires spread the load on lawns and soft ground, which cuts down on ruts.
The same approach works in woodlots for skidding firewood logs to a landing.
A hauler like this also reduces how much bucking you need to do on site, since you can move longer pieces to a spot where they are easier to process or load.

Buck logs to a size you can control, especially on slopes. Keep feet and hands clear of the tongs and the log, and never try to stop a rolling load with your body. Check tongs and pins for wear before each use.

Plan your path before you lift: look for curbs, slopes, soft spots, and obstacles. Keep the tires inflated to the recommended pressure, grease pivot points, and store the hauler out of the weather so it is ready for the next job.
Follow LogRite's guidance on load limits. Browse more log handling tools.

faq.q: What does a log arch do?
faq.a: It lifts one end of a log off the ground so it rolls on wheels instead of dragging, which takes much less effort.

faq.q: Why wide tires?
faq.a: Wide tires float better on lawns, mud, and sand, and leave fewer ruts on clients' yards.

name: CMI LCD Lowering Control Device
title: CMI Lowering Control Device (LCD) for Rigging
meta: The CMI lowering control device (LCD) adds friction to a rigging line so the ground crew can let pieces run and stop them smoothly. Setup notes and price.
tagline: Friction device that helps the ground crew control loads on a rigging line.
summary: The CMI lowering control device (LCD) adds friction to the rigging line so the ground crew can let a piece run and bring it to a controlled stop. It anchors to the tree or a solid point and takes the heat off the groundie's hands.
highlights: Friction device for rigging lines
Gives the ground crew control of loads
Anchors to the tree or a suitable anchor
Reduces hand fatigue on long days

p: When a piece is cut and falls into the rigging, the line needs friction to slow and stop it. Wrapping a rope around a tree trunk works, but it wears the bark and the rope and the friction is hard to adjust. A lowering device gives a set number of wraps on a dedicated surface, so the operator can feed or hold with steady control.
That control matters for letting a piece run so it does not shock-load the rigging point.
The ground crew can also use it to hold a piece in place while the climber repositions, then lower it in a controlled way to a clear landing spot.

Anchor the device as CMI's instructions specify, use a rope diameter it is designed for, and match the friction to the load. The whole system, from rigging point to anchor, must be rated for the forces involved, and dynamic loads can far exceed the weight of the piece.

Inspect the device for grooves, cracks, and sharp edges before each job, and retire the rigging line if it shows glazing, cuts, or crushed sections. Clear communication between the climber and the ground operator is part of every rigging plan.
Rigging should be planned and run by trained crews. See all lowering devices.

faq.q: What rope works with the CMI LCD?
faq.a: Use a rope diameter within CMI's stated range for the device, and check the instructions for any construction limits.

faq.q: Do I need a lowering device for every removal?
faq.a: Not for small pieces, but when rigging heavier wood a dedicated device gives safer, more consistent control.

name: DMM Pinto Rig Pulley V2
title: DMM Pinto Rig Pulley V2 for Climbing & Rigging
meta: The DMM Pinto Rig pulley V2 is a compact pulley with an extra attachment hole for building climbing and mechanical advantage systems. Uses, notes and price.
tagline: Compact pulley with an extra attachment point for climbing and MA systems.
summary: The DMM Pinto Rig pulley V2 is a compact pulley with an additional attachment point that makes it useful for building mechanical advantage systems, tending a hitch, and setting up SRS and MRS climbing configurations.
highlights: Compact pulley sized for climbing gear
Extra attachment point for system building
Useful for hitch tending and MA systems
Updated V2 design

p: Climbers use the Pinto Rig in several ways: tending a friction hitch, building a 3:1 or 2:1 system to haul gear or pre-tension a line, or setting up a redirect. The extra attachment point lets you clip a hitch, a carabiner, or a second rope component without stacking gear on one carabiner.
It is compact enough to live on the saddle without getting in the way.
A compact pulley that can do several jobs saves weight and clutter on the saddle, which matters on long climbs.

The V2 update keeps the compact size that made the original popular while refining the design. If you already own the original Pinto Rig, check DMM's details for what changed before mixing versions in a system.

Check DMM's specifications for compatible rope diameters and rated loads, and use only locking connectors. When building mechanical advantage, remember that forces at the anchor and pulley increase, so size every component for the load.
Inspect the sheave, side plates, axle, and attachment holes for wear and damage before each use. Retire the pulley if a side plate is cracked, the sheave wobbles, or rope grooves show in the metal.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. See more micro pulleys.

faq.q: What is the extra hole on the Pinto Rig for?
faq.a: It gives a separate attachment point for building systems, such as attaching a hitch or the end of a haul line.

faq.q: Can I use it for rigging wood?
faq.a: It is sized for climbing and light systems. Use rigging blocks rated for the loads when lowering wood.

name: R-Easy Climbing Lanyard Adjusting Pulley
title: R-Easy Climbing Lanyard Adjusting Pulley
meta: The R-Easy is a lanyard adjusting pulley that helps you take in slack on a hitch-based climbing lanyard. How it fits a lanyard setup, safety notes and price.
tagline: Pulley designed to make adjusting a climbing lanyard smoother.
summary: The R-Easy is a lanyard adjusting pulley designed to help a climbing lanyard run smoothly as you take in or let out length. It works where a hitch or adjuster sits on your lanyard, so tending slack takes less effort.
highlights: Pulley for lanyard adjustment
Smoother slack tending
Reduces wear on hitch and lanyard rope
Compact enough for the saddle

body.h: Why add a pulley to your lanyard
p: Lanyard adjustment happens dozens of times on a climb. Without a pulley, rope drags against a carabiner and the hitch has to be pushed by hand. A dedicated pulley lets the tail run more freely so the lanyard self-tends as you shorten it, and it spreads wear away from the carabiner.
That makes repositioning around a stem or limb quicker and less tiring.
Climbers who spend long days repositioning in big canopies often find a pulley-tended lanyard saves noticeable effort over the course of a climb.

Set the pulley up exactly as the manufacturer's instructions show, with the specified rope diameters and connectors, and test the system near the ground before going aloft. Check the sheave turns freely and the side plates show no cracks or grooves.

We list this item as a pre-order product; check availability and current specifications before you buy. Store it clean and dry, keep it away from grit, and retire it after a significant fall or any visible damage.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. Browse more micro pulleys.

faq.q: Will the R-Easy work with any lanyard?
faq.a: Check the manufacturer's rope diameter range and approved setups before fitting it to your lanyard.

faq.q: Do I still need a hitch or adjuster?
faq.a: Yes. The pulley helps tend the lanyard but does not replace the hitch or mechanical adjuster that holds your position.

name: Nylon Loop Runners
title: Nylon Loop Runners: Sewn Slings for Climbers
meta: Nylon loop runners are sewn webbing slings for anchors, redirects, gear storage and quick extensions. How tree climbers use them, inspection notes and price.
tagline: Sewn nylon webbing loops for anchors, redirects, and gear organization.
summary: Nylon loop runners are sewn webbing slings that climbers use to build anchors, set redirects, extend a connection, and organize gear on the saddle. They are light, cheap, and one of the most versatile pieces of soft gear on the harness.
highlights: Sewn nylon webbing loops
Good for anchors and redirects
Extends connections around stems and limbs
Handy for organizing gear

p: A sewn runner can be girth-hitched or basket-hitched around a limb for a redirect, used to extend a connection past bark, or clipped to a saddle ring to carry tools. Nylon has some stretch and handles knots and hitches well.
Several lengths on the saddle let you adapt to different stem sizes without reaching for rope.
Runners also make simple tool lanyards and gear slings, and a few spares in the kit bag cover a lot of small jobs on the climb.

Webbing is easily cut. Keep runners away from saw chains and sharp edges, and out of sun, chemicals, and fuel. Inspect the stitching and webbing before each use and retire any runner that is cut, faded, stiff, or has damaged stitching. Ratings drop when you tie knots or choke a sling, so follow the marked ratings for each configuration.
Mark each runner with its purchase date and keep track of its age, since webbing loses strength over time even without visible damage. Store runners clean and dry with the rest of your soft gear.
Life-support gear must meet the applicable standard (ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions), be inspected before every use, and be used only by trained climbers. More climbing gear is here.

faq.q: Nylon or Dyneema runners?
faq.a: Nylon is cheaper, stretches a little, and tolerates knots. Dyneema is lighter and stronger for its width but has a lower melting point and is less suited to knots.

faq.q: Can I use a runner as a cambium saver?
faq.a: Only if the manufacturer approves that use. A purpose-built friction saver is better for a climbing line.
